## 🎓 4‑Week Deep‑Learning Roadmap **Domain:** Deep Learning **Level:** Advanced‑Beginner **Year:** 4th Year (College) **Dept:** AI & Data Science (AIDS) > **Goal:** Turn your “advanced‑beginner” knowledge into a **portfolio‑ready skill set** that will make you stand out in campus placements, internships, and entry‑level AI roles. --- ## 1️⃣ Overview & Learning Goals | ✅ Goal | 📌 Why it matters for placement | |--------|--------------------------------| | **Master a DL framework** (PyTorch **or** TensorFlow) | Most job postings require hands‑on experience with one of them. | | **Implement end‑to‑end pipelines** (data prep → model → evaluation → deployment) | Shows you can ship a product, not just a notebook. | | **Build 2‑3 portfolio projects** (see Capstone ideas) | Recruiters love GitHub repos with clear READMEs, notebooks, and results. | | **Learn the math that matters** (linear algebra, probability, optimization) | Deep‑learning interviews often probe fundamentals. | | **Get comfortable with the current research trends** (Transformers, Diffusion, RL) | Signals you can keep up with the fast‑moving field. | --- ## 2️⃣ Week‑by‑Week Breakdown > **Tip:** Allocate **~15 h/week** (2 h/day + 1 h weekend deep‑dive). Adjust if you have more/less time. ### 📅 **Week 1 – Foundations & Framework Setup** | Day | Topics | Resources | Mini‑Task | |-----|--------|-----------|-----------| | Mon‑Tue | **Python refresher** – NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, seaborn | • *Python Data Science Handbook* (Jake VanderPlas) – free on GitHub
• **DataCamp** “Intro to Python for Data Science” (free first chapter) | Load the **UCI Wine** dataset, explore with pandas, plot pair‑plots. | | Wed‑Thu | **Linear Algebra & Calculus** – vectors, matrix ops, chain rule, gradient descent | • 3Blue1Brown **Essence of Linear Algebra** (YouTube)
• **MIT OCW** 18.06 Linear Algebra (lecture 1‑3) | Derive the gradient of a simple MSE loss and implement it from scratch. | | Fri | **Probability & Statistics** – distributions, Bayes, hypothesis testing | • *StatQuest* YouTube playlist (Statistics Basics)
• **Khan Academy** “Probability” (selected videos) | Simulate a Gaussian mixture and plot its PDF. | | Sat‑Sun | **Framework choice & environment** – install PyTorch **or** TensorFlow, set up VS Code + Jupyter, create a GitHub repo “dl‑roadmap‑starter”. | • Official **PyTorch** tutorial: *Getting Started*
• **TensorFlow** “TensorFlow in Practice” (Coursera – free audit)
• **GitHub Docs** “Hello World” guide | Clone the **mlacademyai/Machine-Learning-Roadmap** repo, add a `README.md` with your learning plan. | **Deliverable:** A **Jupyter notebook** titled `Week1_Foundations.ipynb` uploaded to GitHub, with data‑exploration, math derivations, and a “Hello‑World” NN (single linear layer) in your chosen framework. --- ### 📅 **Week 2 – Core Deep‑Learning Blocks** | Day | Topics | Resources | Mini‑Task | |-----|--------|-----------|-----------| | Mon‑Tue | **Neural‑Network basics** – perceptron, activation functions, back‑prop, loss, optimizers | • *Deep Learning A‑Z™* (Udemy – first 2 sections)
• **Fast.ai** “Practical Deep Learning for Coders” (Lesson 1) | Re‑implement **binary classification** on the **Breast Cancer Wisconsin** dataset using a 2‑layer MLP from scratch (no high‑level API). | | Wed‑Thu | **Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)** – conv layers, pooling, padding, common architectures (LeNet, AlexNet) | • **CS231n** Stanford (lecture 1‑3) – free videos
• **PyTorch** tutorial “Transfer Learning for Computer Vision” | Train a CNN on **CIFAR‑10** (use data augmentation). Log training curves with TensorBoard. | | Fri | **Regularization & Optimization** – dropout, batch‑norm, learning‑rate schedules, Adam, early stopping | • **DeepLearning.AI** “Improving Deep Neural Networks” (Coursera – free audit)
• **Paper** “Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization” (read abstract + key equations) | Add dropout & batch‑norm to the CIFAR‑10 model; compare validation accuracy. | | Sat‑Sun | **Project checkpoint** – write a short blog post (Markdown) summarizing Week 2 learnings, push to GitHub Pages. | • **GitHub Pages** guide (official)
• **Medium** “How to Write a Technical Blog” (free) | Publish `week2_cnn.md` with plots, code snippets, and reflections. | **Deliverable:** GitHub repo now contains **two notebooks**, a **blog post**, and a **trained CNN model** (`cifar10_cnn.pth` or `.h5`). --- ### 📅 **Week 3 – Specialized Architectures & Modern Trends** | Day | Topics | Resources | Mini‑Task | |-----|--------|-----------|-----------| | Mon‑Tue | **Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN, LSTM, GRU)** – sequence modeling, teacher forcing | • **DeepLearning.AI** “Sequence Models” (Coursera – free audit)
• **PyTorch** tutorial “Language Modeling with RNNs” | Build a character‑level language model on **Shakespeare** text; generate 200‑char sample. | | Wed‑Thu | **Transformers & Attention** – self‑attention, positional encoding, BERT, GPT‑2 basics | • **The Illustrated Transformer** (Jay Alammar)
• **Hugging Face** “Course – Transformers 101” (free) | Fine‑tune **DistilBERT** on the **IMDB Sentiment** dataset (use 🤗 `datasets` library). | | Fri | **Generative Models** – GANs, VAEs, Diffusion basics | • **NVIDIA** “GANs in Action” YouTube series
• **Fast.ai** “Generative Deep Learning” (lesson 7) | Train a **DCGAN** to generate MNIST digits; visualize generated images after each epoch. | | Sat‑Sun | **MLOps mini‑pipeline** – model versioning (DVC), containerization (Docker), simple API (FastAPI) | • **DVC** docs – “Getting Started”
• **Docker** tutorial “Python + FastAPI” (FreeCodeCamp) | Containerize the DistilBERT sentiment model and expose a `/predict` endpoint. | **Deliverable:** Add three new folders: `rnn_lstm/`, `transformers/`, `gan/` with notebooks, model files, and a **Dockerfile** for the API. --- ### 📅 **Week 4 – Portfolio Polish & Interview Prep** | Day | Topics | Resources | Mini‑Task | |-----|--------|-----------|-----------| | Mon‑Tue | **Model Evaluation & Explainability** – ROC‑AUC, confusion matrix, SHAP, Grad‑CAM | • **scikit‑learn** docs – “Model evaluation”
• **SHAP** tutorial (official)
• **Grad‑CAM** PyTorch repo (GitHub) | Produce a **report** (PDF) comparing CNN vs. Transformer on CIFAR‑10 (accuracy, FLOPs, inference time). | | Wed‑Thu | **Resume & Portfolio Building** – writing project descriptions, linking GitHub, creating a personal site | • **DataCamp** “Data Scientist Portfolio” (free article)
• **Canva** resume templates (free) | Update LinkedIn with 2 project highlights; add a **“Projects”** section on your personal site. | | Fri | **Mock Technical Interview** – whiteboard NN math, coding on a shared editor (CodiMD), system design basics | • **Interview Query** “Deep Learning Interview Questions” (free)
• **Pramp** (peer‑to‑peer mock interviews) | Solve 2 interview‑style questions: (a) Derive back‑prop for a single neuron; (b) Design a scalable image‑tagging service. | | Sat‑Sun | **Capstone Selection & Planning** – choose one of the three capstone ideas (see below), outline milestones, create a GitHub project board. | • **Trello** or GitHub Projects (free) | Draft a **2‑page proposal** (problem, data, model, evaluation) and commit it to the repo. | **Deliverable:** A **complete portfolio repo** (`deep-learning-portfolio/`) with: * All notebooks & trained models * Dockerized API for at least one model * Evaluation report PDF * Resume & project page links --- ## 3️⃣ Core Skills Checklist | ✅ Skill | ✔️ Mastered? | 📚 Resource | |----------|--------------|------------| | Python (NumPy, pandas, matplotlib) | | Python Data Science Handbook | | Linear Algebra & Calculus basics | | 3Blue1Brown, MIT OCW | | Probability & Statistics fundamentals | | StatQuest, Khan Academy | | PyTorch **or** TensorFlow (core API) | | Official tutorials | | Back‑propagation & gradient descent | | Deep Learning A‑Z, CS231n | | CNN architecture & image pipelines | | CS231n, PyTorch Transfer Learning | | RNN/LSTM/GRU for sequences | | DeepLearning.AI Sequence Models | | Transformer & attention mechanisms | | The Illustrated Transformer, Hugging Face Course | | GAN/VAEs basics | | NVIDIA GAN series | | Model evaluation (metrics, confusion matrix, ROC‑AUC) | | scikit‑learn docs | | Explainability (SHAP, Grad‑CAM) | | SHAP tutorial | | MLOps basics (DVC, Docker, FastAPI) | | DVC docs, Docker tutorial | | Git & GitHub best practices (README, issues, CI) | | GitHub Docs | | Communication (technical blog, resume) | | DataCamp Portfolio article | | Interview problem‑solving (math & coding) | | Interview Query DL Q&A | Mark each ✔️ as you complete the week‑tasks. --- ## 4️⃣ Capstone Project Ideas (Pick ONE) | # | Title & Problem | Why It Impresses Recruiters | Suggested Stack | |---|------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------| | **1️⃣ Medical Image Classification** | Build a **binary classifier** to detect pneumonia from chest X‑ray images (e.g., NIH ChestX‑ray14). | Shows ability to handle real‑world, high‑stakes data; includes preprocessing, class imbalance, and model interpretability. | PyTorch, `torchvision` transforms, Grad‑CAM for explainability, Docker + FastAPI for inference, DVC for data versioning. | | **2️⃣ Multilingual Chatbot with Retrieval‑Augmented Generation** | Create a **customer‑support chatbot** that answers FAQs in English & Hindi using a hybrid RAG pipeline (BM25 retrieval + fine‑tuned DistilGPT‑2). | Demonstrates mastery of NLP, large‑language‑model fine‑tuning, and deployment of a production‑grade API. | Hugging Face 🤗 Transformers, FAISS for vector search, FastAPI, Docker, GitHub Actions CI. | | **3️⃣ Diffusion‑Based Art Generator** | Train a **Stable Diffusion**‑style model on a custom dataset of campus‑themed illustrations and expose a web UI for on‑the‑fly image generation. | Highlights knowledge of cutting‑edge generative models, GPU optimization, and UI/UX for AI products. | PyTorch + Diffusers library, Streamlit front‑end, GPU‑accelerated training on Google Colab Pro, Docker. | *Pick one, break it into 4‑week milestones (data collection → baseline → improvement → deployment) and showcase it on GitHub + a personal site.* --- ## 5️⃣ Pro Tips for the Deep‑Learning Domain 1. **Focus on one framework first** – become *very* comfortable with PyTorch **or** TensorFlow before hopping. 2. **Version‑control data** with **DVC**; recruiters love seeing reproducible pipelines. 3. **Write a clear README**: problem statement, data source, model architecture diagram, results, and how to run the code. 4. **Add a “Results” section** with plots and a short discussion; treat it like a mini‑paper. 5. **Participate in a Kaggle micro‑competition** (e.g., “Titanic” or “House Prices”) – you’ll get a public leaderboard badge for your resume. 6. **Network on LinkedIn & Discord** – join groups like *“Deep Learning Researchers”* or *“AI for Healthcare”* and share your weekly progress. 7. **Practice whiteboard math** – derive the gradient of a Conv2D layer on paper; interviewers love it. 8. **Stay current** – allocate **30 min every Sunday** to read the *“Paper of the Week”* on arXiv (e.g., a recent Vision Transformer or Diffusion paper). --- ### 🚀 Ready, Set, Deploy! Start the week by cloning the **mlacademyai/Machine-Learning-Roadmap** repo, create your own fork, and follow the schedule above. By the end of four weeks you’ll have: * A polished GitHub portfolio with **four end‑to‑end notebooks** and a **Dockerized API**. * A **technical blog post** and updated **resume** ready for campus placement drives. * A concrete capstone plan that you can finish over the next 2‑3 months and showcase in interviews. Good luck, and remember: **consistency beats intensity** – a little bit each day builds a powerful AI career foundation! 🎉

## ATS Score (out of 100)  
**Estimated Score: 62 / 100**

**Why:**  
* **Positive points** – The resume contains many relevant technical keywords (Python, React, FastAPI, AWS, TensorFlow, LangChain, etc.), a clear education section, and quantifiable achievements (e.g., “94% accuracy”, “Top 8.5% LeetCode”).  
* **Deduction reasons** –  
  * Inconsistent date formats and overlapping timelines confuse parsers.  
  * Sections are not clearly delimited with standard headings (e.g., “ACHIEVEMENTS: Skills:” merges two sections).  
  * Contact line mixes email, phone, location, LinkedIn, and GitHub without labels, making it hard for ATS to extract.  
  * Bullet points sometimes start with lower‑case letters or lack a verb, reducing readability for automated scoring.  
  * Too many abbreviations and jargon without expansion (e.g., “RAG”, “LLM”) can be missed if the ATS is not trained on them.  

---

## Strengths  

| Area | What’s Working Well |
|------|----------------------|
| **Quantified Impact** | “Delivered 100% accurate and timely responses”, “94% accuracy”, “Top 8.5% LeetCode, 777+ problems” – concrete numbers catch both human reviewers and ATS. |
| **Relevant Technical Stack** | Heavy focus on modern SDE‑relevant tools: Python, React, FastAPI, Docker, AWS, MongoDB, LangChain, LangGraph, FAISS, Redis. |
| **Research & ML Experience** | Projects on music‑genre classification, anxiety detection, and multi‑agent LLM systems demonstrate depth in AI/ML, valuable for “advanced” SDE roles that involve AI products. |
| **Leadership & Soft Skills** | Scout captain, hackathon finalist, and competition organizer show initiative and teamwork – good for culture fit. |
| **Certifications** | AWS Cloud Practitioner, AWS Machine Learning Associate, IBM DB & SQL – adds credibility to cloud/DB knowledge. |

---

## Gaps & Weaknesses  

| Issue | Explanation |
|-------|-------------|
| **Date inconsistencies & future dates** | Internships listed up to 2025 (e.g., “FullStack Developer Intern … 14/07/2025–05/09/2025”) are in the future relative to today (2026). This raises suspicion and confuses ATS chronology. |
| **Mixed/Unclear Section Titles** | “ACHIEVEMENTS: Skills:” merges two distinct sections; “Certifications” appears after “Tools” without a heading break. |
| **Thin Descriptions for Some Roles** | The “Data Analyst Intern” bullet points are generic (“optimized ETL workflows”) without specifics on tools, data volume, or performance gains. |
| **Redundant / Over‑loaded Bullets** | Several bullets repeat the same idea (e.g., multiple mentions of “multi‑agent” and “LLM”). Consolidate for brevity. |
| **Missing Core SDE Fundamentals** | No explicit mention of algorithms & data structures implementation beyond “DSA‑focused” in CodeChef. No evidence of system design, scalability testing, or CI/CD pipelines (aside from GitHub Actions). |
| **Lack of Production‑grade Metrics** | No mention of production deployment, latency, throughput, or cost savings – metrics that senior SDE roles love. |
| **Formatting errors** | Inconsistent bullet symbols (mix of “•” and “-”), random line breaks, and missing spaces after periods make parsing harder. |
| **Spelling / Grammar** | Typos such as “Al‑powered”, “per first year”, “Fundametals”, “Computing Everywhere.” |
| **Over‑use of Acronyms** | Terms like “RAG”, “LLM”, “FAISS” are not expanded; ATS may miss them if they are not part of its dictionary. |
| **No “Summary” or “Objective”** | A short headline that aligns with the target SDE role is missing. |

* Keep each bullet ≤ 2 lines for ATS readability.

## Formatting & Structure Tips  

1. **Header** – Use a single line:  
   `JASHWANTH KV | +91‑9342410206 | jeshwanthkv.aids2023@citchennai.net | Chennai, India | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/jashwanthkv | GitHub: github.com/Jashwanthkv`  

2. **Consistent Date Format** – Use `Month YYYY – Month YYYY` (e.g., `May 2023 – Jun 2023`). Avoid day numbers unless necessary.  

3. **Section Headings** – Use bold H2 (`## Education`, `## Experience`, `## Projects`, `## Skills`, `## Certifications`, `## Volunteering`).  

4. **Bullet Style** – Use plain hyphens (`-`) or Unicode bullets, but keep them uniform.  

5. **One‑Page Length** – Trim redundant wording; aim for ≤ 1 page (or 2 pages max if you have > 5 years experience).  

6. **Skills Table** – Create a concise table with categories (Programming Languages, Frameworks, Cloud, Databases, Tools).  

7. **Quantify Every Bullet** – Add numbers, percentages, or time savings wherever possible.  

8. **Proofread** – Run spell‑check; fix “Al‑powered”, “per first year”, “Fundametals”, “Computing Everywhere”.  

9. **Remove Future Dates** – Replace any 2025/2026 internships with actual completed experiences or label them as “Upcoming (Planned)”.  

10. **Avoid Over‑loading Lines** – Break long sentences into two bullets if they contain more than one idea.
